So I had hoped to be able to write something better, but I can't in the state the game is currently.  As I have said in reviews in the past, Early Release does not mean Beta Test.  I understand that the idea of an early release is that there might be a few things to tweak, but not bugs upon bugs.  This should have been taken care of in a 'beta', not in a 'this is ready for public consumption'.  Without further ado here are a few things that stopped me dead in my tracks.

[u]Things That Didn't Work[/u]
1) Guests are running into eachother: Game breaking pathing should not be a thing at the public consumption stage.  When two guests run into eachother into a hallway and continue to walk into eachother and never leave the hotel, that is a bit oversight.  Two rooms are now off the market.  Sure I could try to find a workaround to see if I can't kick people out of the hotel, but i shouldn't need to go to that extreme with a released product
2) Maids leaving with linen: Yup.  That was a thing.  So if you have a room being cleaned and it hits 2200h, the twits will walk out of the hotel and go to their minivan with the linen that they just washed and they don't come back with the linen.  In fact they will come back into the hotel and stand in the room like a moron wondering where the linen was.  Room is dirty, I can't get linen on the bed, and so yup, gonna take a hit.  Again, how is this a thing.
3) Take a long time to decorate: Decoration for a room takes a long long time.  It is not very streamlined.  This is especially annoying with the damn bell going off every few seconds.  So doing about 1.5 rooms takes me most of the day and I will be yawning like a crazy person and have to pause my work cause I can't see anything
4) Yawning all the time: I get it dude.  It's 2200h, you are a bit tired..., but suck it up Twila, you have some work to do.  The non-stop yawning and vision blurring makes me want to smack a llama.  I have work to do buddy, shut up..., nope here he goes again.  I find this part triggered me a lot.

[u]Things That Could Have Been Better[/u]
1) The Lobby: You enter the hotel and it felt..., blah.  I honestly didn't give a crap about the place.  There is a hotel design game that starts you in the lobby in terms of giving that a facelift.  I think that that would have been a good place to start making you care about the hotel, and also other people coming into it.  Having some sort of tutorial that starts with that to teach you about design, placement, coloring, etc would have been a good touch.  First impression leaves a lasting impact on a customer, and I have seen bit rate hotels leave me with a better taste than the lobby in this game.
2) More accessible laundry room: Having to run downstairs instead of having your 'cleaning' room readily accessible for you/staff, for me that is annoying and I think that this would have had a better feel and taste.
3) Weird room placement: This is just my OCD speaking, but opening rooms 6-9 instead of starting with 1 and going onwards, this bugged me.  This is just me, but I would have felt better if they would have let me start with room 1 and move onwards.  Not a deal breaker, but this is just something that would have made me feel better

At the end of the day, the bugs, and the time it takes to decorate are the cake.  The icing on that cake is the yawning.  The first three are things that should have been taken care of, and if people are going to say 'its early release', no these are Beta Testing things that should have been covered in that phase.  If you go buy a car and find out that you can't ever turn left in it, and find out it can't be fixed for the next 6 months while they order hardware, that's a big problem and it's not a 'your turning signal sometimes doesn't work' kind of an oopsie that can be handled in the wash down the road.  If the auto industry can't sell that, then what the heck are we doing with games clearly not ready for play.  But that yawning makes me put the game away.  I want to try this down the road and I hope to be able to re-review it and give it a thumbs up.  But the ingredients that they put into the cake, didn't really turn out well when it was done the baking process.  In my opinion, it's not ready for purchase, and I would wait for a while to see if they fix it enough for it to be truly ready for public consumption.

I bought the game because I like games of this genre, which I've played countless times, and the graphics and interactivity from the developers were quite promising.
But I didn't know that it was possible to ruin a promising game like that.
So, I'll go straight to the disadvantages.

1. The inventory doesn't close with the same button, needed to look for Escape. This is always inconvenient, and in conditions of increased danger, when you can be shot at from any side at any time, this is clearly meanness on the part of the developers.

2. The font of the information messages is small and dirty.

3. To chop a tree with a sickle, and even stone and ore? The logic is fantastic. Well, in that case it was necessary to make it at least a laser sword from Star Wars.

4. But small trees and bushes aren't cut down by anything, they just exist.

5. There is no auto-battle for holding down the mouse button, you need to constantly click.

6. CAMPFIRE!!! They had to manage to make crafting a basic item so counterintuitive. I fiddled with its creation until night (when I just moved on to the next task of going to kill zombies). First I looked in crafting, and, of course, I didn’t find it. Then I created all the items in crafting according to the logic that the campfire will open only after crafting all the previous items, and, of course, I was defeated in the fight against the mind-blowing logic of the developers. Then I cut down all the trees in the area, because I assumed that the creation of a campfire was conditional on the presence of a large amount of wood. Then I threw wood and fat on the ground in the hope of setting them on fire - but only with anal fire, because I'd neither a lighter nor a firearm. Then I went online for a guide (I'll say it again, they really had to try to complicate a simple task like that), found it, because it turns out that I'm far from the first one to start looking for this information (which is good, because in this game I was already starting to doubt my own sanity), and found out that, according to the developers' logic, a fire is a type of house, so its creation is in construction menu. I started clicking on creation and, of course, was defeated again. I looked at the creation conditions - this includes stones, which I had happily spent on useless crafting of the previous things. Okay, I chopped up some stones with our laser Jedi sickle, chose a suitable place for a campfire pit for the umpteenth time and started clicking on the creation of a fire again, and, of course, was defeated again - was it possible to expect a different result? It turns out that a campfire cannot be made in a "safe" zone, i.e. near the campsite (I still don't understand why it's safe, because zombies and cleaners run around and kill freely there, including indoors, while the sellers look at them with frostbitten eyes - point 7) - needed to go further into the wild zone, closer to the warm friendly company of zombies and cleaners.

I went to clean up the zombies, almost died, because can create bandages only from the skin of killed animals (point 8) - the clothes of killed zombies and even cleaners aren't suitable (not feng shui, not kosher, haram, and in general not according to the concepts of brutal guys - only hardcore), finally convinced myself that we clearly have different logical paths with the developers and returned the game.

I really wanted to like Dreadzone. It has a gritty, post-apocalyptic vibe concept that could’ve been a hit—but right out of the gate, the pacing felt slow and uninspired. The intro tasks dragged, and it took far too long to get to anything engaging.

Once I started exploring more, a few things stood out in a frustrating way:

Cons:

Enemies are tanky and respawn way too quickly—sometimes before I could even finish looting. They weren’t challenging, just annoying.

Weapon selection early on is extremely limited: just a knife and a pistol. And with no HUD ammo counter, I had to constantly open the inventory to check.

The AI followed me for unexpectedly long distances, which felt unbalanced.

Human combat encounters felt stale and repetitive.

Even after adjusting DLSS, resolution, and other settings, the graphics still left a lot to be desired.

I only played on keyboard and mouse, so I can’t speak to controller support.

Pros:

The concept has potential. There’s a solid foundation here if the devs continue to refine and build on it.

I'm willing to leave my purchase as a donation to the developers in the hope they can turn this into something special over time.

Final thoughts:
Dreadzone feels like it needed more time in development. I’ll check back on it periodically, but as it stands now, I’m having a hard time finding the motivation to keep playing. I truly hope the team puts everything they’ve got into polishing it up—because there’s a chance this could grow into a game worth the time and money.

My Feedback on the Game (Survival-Based Game):

The idea of the game is great, especially as a survival game that resembles other titles in the genre. However, the technical issues are many and they ruin the experience.

The character movement, such as walking and running, needs improvement—it feels clunky and unpolished.

All zombie sounds are the same, which kills the immersion. It would be much more enjoyable if each zombie had unique sounds or traits that set them apart.

Loot crates often contain items that aren’t useful. It would be more rewarding if, after fighting through a horde of enemies in a cave or an abandoned place, I found a loot box that actually gave me a good weapon or armor as a reward.

The world lacks points of interest to explore—besides trees, there’s not much to see or interact with.

The cover system (crouching while aiming) doesn’t really add any strategic benefit.


Overall, the game has a lot of potential, but right now it's held back by these issues. This is just my opinion, and I truly hope to see improvements and updates in the future.

It's not a bad Tribes game. There just isn't anything to do in the game if you aren't very good at 3D dueling combat or flag capping/chasing.

Past Tribes games had large maps, large bases, vehicles to pilot, an array of deployable items so you could base build, etc. T1/T2 also had mods with much more of these gameplay aspects.

This game has small maps with open flags, small bases, no vehicles, and no way to play a dedicated base building role.

Developers (as usual) don't understand what makes a Tribes game easy or hard, so they have tried to make an easy Tribes game while actually making a hard one.

There are also currently hit detection bugs, but this would be more so expected for early access.

This may be a fun game for veterans of the Tribes series, but it's difficult to recommend it to anybody else at all.

For now, the game just isn’t worth the money. 

There are quite a few unfinished parts, especially in the Polish translation – many things are simply translated wrong (for example, Grapefruit as Winogrona [Grapes], Chips as Chipy [?]).
It’s a 10-hour game at most. After that, everything is maxed out. Each club takes around 3–4 nights before you move to the next one.

The first two clubs are pretty fun. There’s a lot to learn and do - one person takes orders, another mixes drinks, someone else cooks food, and another serves customers. Everyone has a clear role, no one gets lost, and it’s genuinely enjoyable.

The third club, though, feels completely disconnected from the rest. It’s the least polished and simply not enjoyable. There are only a few drinks and a bunch of drugs. Most of the work falls on one person handling the orders, while the rest just stand around bored. Customers order a ton, and the order board text is so long it constantly scrolls – meaning you waste time waiting for it to loop back just to check if you've prepared a correct order. It’s easily the most frustrating part of the game. The person at the bar ends up doing everything, while the "warehouse" crew have nothing to do. This club really needs better task distribution so one person isn’t overloaded.
Also, I really missed the cigarette stand that was in the demo. A separate stand would’ve helped balance the gameplay a lot.

Another issue: personal money. You can buy all the character customization options super fast – and there’s not much of it anyway. A few hairstyles, a few clothes, in mostly black color, and that’s it. Once you buy everything, there’s no reason to keep earning money. That's when the game gets boring.

On the positive side, the game offers funny moments, such as a llama or bizarre customers, which add some humor and lightness to the experience.

For starters, the little screen you see the orders on is just bad in so many ways. It scrolls constantly (and not in a continuous way, like it hops back constantly), when you have an order that's a little too long to fit on the screen.
It only holds up to 3 orders at a time.
The orders, once you upgrade to the club and get food as well, are extremely intricate, too much if you ask me. 
The very very little time you get from the customers before they get mad. That's at the bar as well as when they've put an order in.
The bottles for all the drinks holds and insanely small amount of liquid. Like a gin holds 4 servings... I wouldn't mind paying more for a bottle if it meant I didn't have to throw one out and get a new one every 30 seconds.
Once you upgrade to the second club there are sooo many drinks, which also just makes it less fun 'cus you can't remember all of them and (I at least) have to spend a lot of time looking at the board to find out what I'm making. You should perhaps be able to choose which drinks you're serving - and perhaps also if you're a club that serves food or not. That would make it more playable for more people I would think.
Many orders (double and even triple checked several times) ended up failing with the customer for "being wrong". 
Many surfaces and cupboards you aren't able to place things on/in.
There's no indication of what order number is currently on your tray.
It also sucks that any tiny order must be on a tray to serve it, especially because the tray serves no purpose, when it's just a drink, without the order number.
The UI when you're on the different screens is very inconsistent. Like the back button is never really the same.

Having to keep up with all these things, taking orders, making food, making drinks, while doing the dishes, and fighting the occasional customer... just makes it a bit too much for me at least.

As I said, some smaller, some bigger issues.

The gimmicks are funny and it had so much potential. But these things all put together, just make it extremely hard to enjoy...
I've been looking forward to it for a long time, so this really sucks. Perhaps it'll be better in the future with updates to the way many of their current game mechanics work.
